results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

This is a policy decision, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. args.query: Why can't I sell my CBD candle on Google?

response.query: Why can't I sell my CBD candle on Google?

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: Could some automatic setting fill in the missing barcodes for me?
turns.reply:
No, automatic item updates do not cover missing product barcode numbers (GTIN). According to [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284), automatic updates only cover price, sale price, availability, and condition.

To fix the missing product barcode number (GTIN) warning, you need to add the correct barcode number to your product data. Here are the affected products:
- HG-002: "Linen Napkins, Set of 4, Natural"
- HG-007: "Wool Throw Blanket, Charcoal Herringbone"

According to [Product barcode number (GTIN)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324461), a GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier, and never make one up. If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one; send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead, or use the identifier exists setting if the product truly has no identifiers at all, as explained in [Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324478).

After you update your products, Google checks them again, which usually finishes within 24 to 48 hours, as described in [What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802).

Would you like to move on to the next issue?

turns.merchant: Is this one serious?
turns.reply:
Your account has no account-level issues, 5 active products, 0 disapproved products, and 2 warnings for missing product barcode numbers (GTIN).

For your product "Linen Napkins, Set of 4, Natural" (ID: HG-002), the issue is a missing product barcode number (GTIN). According to [Product barcode number (GTIN)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324461), a GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long, and you should copy the number exactly from the packaging or your supplier. If the product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one, but send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead. Alternatively, if the product has no unique product identifiers at all, the [Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324478) doc explains that you can set the identifier exists setting to "no".

Once you correct your product data and upload it again, checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, as outlined in [What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802).

This feature can help avoid price mismatches by automatically updating your product information using what it finds on your website's structured data.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: Why was my cushion cover disapproved?
turns.reply:
Your account has no account issues. You have 1 disapproved product, and 3 products are active.

The product "Velvet Cushion Cover, 18 x 18, Rust" (ID: HG-012) is disapproved because of an availability mismatch: your feed says it is in stock, but your product page says it is out of stock ([Availability in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12470049)).

To fix this, change the availability in your product data to match your product page so they are the same, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk. After you update your products, Google checks them again, which usually finishes within 24 to 48 hours ([What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802)). Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match, the product shows again ([Availability in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12470049)).

Since automatic availability updates are currently turned off for your account, you can also turn on automatic item updates under Products on the Automations tab by choosing an automation and opening View details, which helps avoid mismatches by updating your product information using what Google finds on your website ([Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284)).

Would you like to move on?

Since your automatic price updates are currently turned off, you should also consider turning on automatic item updates as described in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284) to help avoid these mismatches automatically.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
Your account has no account-level issues. However, you have 13 disapproved products and 6 warnings for missing product barcode numbers (GTIN). Here is the breakdown of your disapprovals by the number of products they affect:

1. **Price mismatch**: 3 products.
2. **Invalid image**: 3 products.
3. **Title too long**: 2 products.
4. **Availability mismatch**: 2 products.
5. **Missing shipping**: 2 products.
6. **Restricted product**: 1 product.

You also have 6 products with a warning for missing product barcode numbers (GTIN).

Let's start with the biggest group of disapprovals: **Price mismatch**. This affects the following products:
- **Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage** (HG-004): Feed price is 32.00 USD but the product page shows 36.00 USD.
- **Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper** (HG-015): Feed price is 58.00 USD but the product page shows 64.00 USD.
- **Stainless Steel Kettle, 1.7 L** (HG-021): Feed price is 48.00 USD but the product page shows 44.00 USD.

According to [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029), the price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data ([Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029)). 

Since your automatic price updates are currently turned off, you can also check [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284), which explains that Merchant Center can update price and availability automatically using structured data on your website if you choose to turn it on.

Would you like to move on to the next issue?

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.

turns.merchant: Can I just edit the CBD candle's description to get it approved?
turns.reply:
No, you cannot edit the description to get the CBD candle approved. As explained in [CBD and other unapproved substances](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6165956), products containing cannabidiol (CBD) are on Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements and are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings. This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy. If you disagree with this decision, you can request a review or appeal as described in [Requesting a review or appealing a decision](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13585221), but please note that you may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts.

turns.merchant: What's wrong with my products?
turns.reply:
Your account has no issues. However, 13 products are disapproved and 6 products have warnings.

Here are your disapproved products by the number of products each issue affects:

1. **Price mismatch (3 products):** The feed price does not match the price shown on your website.
- HG-004 "Waffle Weave Bath Towel, Sage": Feed price is 32.00 USD but the product page shows 36.00 USD.
- HG-015 "Pour Over Coffee Set, Glass and Copper": Feed price is 58.00 USD but the product page shows 64.00 USD.
- HG-021 "Stainless Steel Kettle, 1.7 L": Feed price is 48.00 USD but the product page shows 44.00 USD.

2. **Invalid image (3 products):** The image link is missing or points to a placeholder.
- HG-006 "Ceramic Table Lamp, Matte White": No image link is set.
- HG-013 "Walnut Wall Shelf, 24 inch": Image link 'https://cdn.hearthandhollow.example/img/placeholder.png' points to a placeholder, not a real product photo.
- HG-027 "Woven Wall Hanging, Cream and Rust": No image link is set.

3. **Title too long (2 products):** The title exceeds the 150-character limit.
- HG-009 "Handwoven Seagrass Storage Basket with Leather Handles for Living Room, Bedroom, Nursery, Laundry and Bathroom Organization, Extra Large 16 x 12 x 10 inch, Natural Color": Title is 169 characters; the limit is 150.
- HG-017 "Premium Long Staple Egyptian Cotton Sateen Sheet Set, Queen Size, 400 Thread Count, Deep Pocket Fitted Sheet, Flat Sheet and Two Pillowcases, Hotel Quality Bedding in Dove Grey": Title is 176 characters; the limit is 150.

4. **Availability mismatch (2 products):** Feed availability does not match what the product page shows.
- HG-012 "Velvet Cushion Cover, 18 x 18, Rust": Feed says in_stock but the product page says out_of_stock.
- HG-025 "Linen Duvet Cover, Queen, Terracotta": Feed says in_stock but the product page says preorder.

5. **Missing shipping (2 products):** No shipping cost is set.
- HG-019 "Marble Serving Board, White": No shipping cost is set for this product.
- HG-030 "Outdoor String Lights, 48 ft": No shipping cost is set for this product.

6. **Restricted product (1 product):** Mentions a restricted category.
- HG-023 "CBD Infused Lavender Relaxation Candle, 6 oz": Mentions 'CBD', which is a restricted product category.

Additionally, 6 products have a warning for missing product barcode numbers (GTIN) (HG-002, HG-007, HG-011, HG-019, HG-024, HG-028). Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility according to the [Product barcode number (GTIN)](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324461) help doc.

Let's start with your biggest disapproval group: **Price mismatch**. The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency, as explained in the [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029) help doc.

To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days, and once the prices match, the product is approved again.

Your automatic price updates are currently off. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details, as outlined in the [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284) help doc. Note that automatic updates are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products and are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date.

Would you like to move on to the next issue?
